Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Prem Chand, _______ mainly wrote about rural India, was a great Hindi writer.
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'who'.

Key Points

  • That is used in defining clauses.

      • Example: My bike that has a broken seat is in the garage.
  • Whom is simply the objective case of who, which means that it's the form of who that is in the object position in a sentence.
    • Whom केवल who का objective मामला है, जिसका अर्थ है कि यह वह रूप है जो एक वाक्य में object की स्थिति में है।​
      • Example: He saw the faces of those whom he loved at his birthday celebration. 
  • Who is a pronoun, which means that it's used instead of a noun or noun phrase to refer to a noun/noun phrase that has already been mentioned or that does not need to be named specifically.
    • एक सर्वनाम who है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसका उपयोग संज्ञा या संज्ञा वाक्यांश के बजाय एक संज्ञा / संज्ञा वाक्यांश को संदर्भित करने के लिए किया जाता है जिसका पहले ही उल्लेख किया जा चुका है या जिसे विशेष रूप से नाम देने की आवश्यकता नहीं है।​
      • Example: Who is your father?
  • ​Which introduces non-defining clauses.
    • Which का प्रयोग non- defining clauses में किया जाता है।​
      • Example: She seemed more talkative than usual, which was because she was nervous.
  • ​​Correct sentence: Prem Chand, who mainly wrote about rural India, was a great Hindi writer.

Additional Information   

  • Subject pronouns are pronouns that replace the subject in the sentence. 
  • The subject pronouns are we, you, he, she, it, and they.
  • Object pronouns do not replace the subject.
  • Instead, an object pronoun would replace the object in the sentence.
  • The object is the part of the sentence that is being done to, from or with the action.
  • The object pronouns are me, you, him, her, it, us, and them.

🔸 Option C: one sees

  • ✅ Correct

  • Uses correct present tense verb “sees”

  • Matches general tone of the sentence

🔸 Option D: No substitution required

  • ❌ Incorrect

  • “you see” creates a pronoun mismatch with “one”

✅ Final Answer: C. one sees

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This is the author ________ new novel has become an international bestseller.
questions.s:
The context of the sentence is to link an "author" to a "novel" that belongs to them. The blank requires a relative pronoun that indicates possession or ownership.

The correct option is "whose". 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun used to show that something belongs to a person or thing mentioned earlier (in this case, the novel belongs to the author).

The other options do not fit: "who" is a subjective pronoun used to refer to the subject (e.g., the author who writes); "which" is used for things, not people; "whom" is an objective pronoun used to refer to the object.

Thus, the complete sentence is: "This is the author whose new novel has become an international bestseller."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

🔸 Option B: you saw

  • ❌ Incorrect

  • Also keeps the incorrect pronoun "you"

🔸 Option C: one sees

  • Uses correct present tense verb “sees”

questions_hin.q_hi:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

This is the author ________ new novel has become an international bestseller.
questions_hin.s_hi:
The context of the sentence is to link an "author" to a "novel" that belongs to them. The blank requires a relative pronoun that indicates possession or ownership.

The correct option is "whose". 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun used to show that something belongs to a person or thing mentioned earlier (in this case, the novel belongs to the author).

The other options do not fit: "who" is a subjective pronoun used to refer to the subject (e.g., the author who writes); "which" is used for things, not people; "whom" is an objective pronoun used to refer to the object.

Thus, the complete sentence is: "This is the author whose new novel has become an international bestseller."

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions_hin.q_hi:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I, you and she/ have been working happily/ in the same company and in the same branch/ for the last nine years.

questions_hin.s_hi:
The incorrect part is: "I, you and she"

Correct phrase: You, she, and I

The correct order is "Second person (you) → Third person (she/he) → First person (I)" in positive sentences.

So, "I, you and she" should be "You, she, and I."
